128779.q: Your old toy is still good, but you would like something new. What is kind to the environment?
128779.e: When you swap, you have something new to play with, and nothing is thrown away. This way fewer new things are needed.
128779.m: Swapping is better than throwing away.

128780.q: What do you do when you leave a room and nobody else is in it?
128780.e: A light in an empty room uses electricity for nothing. With one click of the switch, you help save energy.
128780.m: When you go out, switch the light off.

128781.q: What do you use to wash dishes clean by hand?
128781.e: Warm water and washing-up liquid loosen grease and food leftovers. Then you rinse the dishes and let them dry.
128781.m: Warm water and washing-up liquid get things clean.

128782.q: Where do your dirty socks belong?
128782.e: In the laundry basket you collect dirty clothes until they are washed. This keeps your room tidy.
128782.m: Dirty laundry goes in the laundry basket.

128783.q: Which animal does the milk you usually buy in the shop come from?
128783.e: Most milk in Switzerland comes from cows. Butter, cheese and yoghurt are also made from milk.
128783.m: Milk usually comes from the cow.

a: Cares for sick people in hospital
128784.e: Polymechanics drill, mill and turn metal parts. They often work with computer-controlled machines.
128784.m: Polymechanics make parts out of metal.

128785.q: What does a healthcare assistant do?
a: Cares for and looks after people in hospital or a care home
128785.e: A healthcare assistant helps sick and elderly people, for example by measuring temperature and blood pressure, and helps with washing and eating.
128785.m: The healthcare assistant looks after people.

a: Furniture and windows out of wood
128786.e: Joiners saw, plane and glue wood. This is how tables, cupboards, doors and windows are made.

128787.q: What does an electrician do in a new house?
a: Lays electric cables and fits sockets
128787.e: Electricians make sure the lights work in a house and that electricity comes out of the sockets. They work very carefully because electricity is dangerous.
128787.m: The electrician brings electricity into the house.

128788.q: Where does a social care worker often work?
a: In a nursery with small children
128788.e: A social care worker plays, does crafts and eats with children at the nursery. Some also look after elderly people or people with disabilities.
128788.m: Social care workers work in nurseries.

a: Plants and looks after flowers, trees and lawns
128789.e: Gardeners work outside with plants. They lay out gardens, cut hedges and mow lawns.

128790.q: What does a retail specialist do in a shop?
a: Advises customers and fills the shelves
128790.e: Retail specialists advise customers, work at the till and make sure the goods are neat and tidy on the shelves.
128790.m: In a shop, retail specialists help you.

128791.q: Where does a cook usually work?
a: In an office full of files
128791.e: Cooks prepare vegetables, fry meat and arrange the food nicely on plates. They work in restaurants, hospitals or canteens.
128791.m: The cook cooks in a restaurant.

128792.q: Who usually pays for the school building you go to?
128792.e: In Switzerland, state schools are paid for with tax money. The municipality usually looks after the school building.
128792.m: My school was built with taxes.

128793.q: Where does your teacher's salary come from?
a: From the children in the class
128793.e: Teachers at state schools are paid with tax money. That way school costs families nothing.

128794.q: Why don't parents have to pay school fees for state school?
a: Because it is paid for with taxes
Because the school is a company
128794.e: State school is free for all children. This is possible because everyone pays taxes together.

128795.q: Mia is playing at the playground in the park. Who usually paid for the slide?
128795.e: Public playgrounds are usually built and looked after by the municipality. The money for this comes from taxes.

128796.q: What are most roads built and repaired with?
128796.e: Roads belong to everyone. The municipality, canton and Confederation pay for them with taxes and other charges.

128797.q: Who pays the police officers' salaries?
a: The people who call for help
128797.e: The police help everyone. That is why they are paid with tax money and not by the people who happen to need help.
128797.m: The police help everyone, and everyone pays.

128798.q: A child calls 117 because they need help. Do they have to pay the police anything afterwards?
a: No, the help is paid for with taxes
Only if it is a Sunday
128798.e: The police are paid with tax money. Anyone in trouble may call 117 and will get help.

128799.q: Which emergency number is for the fire brigade?
128799.e: You can reach the fire brigade on 118. It is organised by the municipality and paid for partly with taxes.
128799.m: If there is a fire, call 118.

128801.q: Lukas borrows a book from the local library. Who helps to pay for the library?
128801.e: Many libraries are supported by the municipality with tax money. That is why borrowing is often free or very cheap for children.
128801.m: Taxes fill the library with books.

128802.q: Why does it often cost only a little to get into the local swimming pool?
a: Because the municipality pays part with taxes
Because the lifeguard works for free
Because the children do the cleaning
128802.e: A swimming pool costs a lot of money. The municipality pays part of it with taxes, so entry is cheap.

128803.q: Who makes sure that the rubbish is collected regularly?
128803.e: The municipality organises rubbish collection. It is paid for with charges, for example for rubbish bags, and partly with taxes.

128804.q: In many municipalities you buy special rubbish bags. Why are they more expensive than normal bags?
a: The price includes a charge for collection
128804.e: With the price of these charged bags you pay part of the rubbish collection. People who make less rubbish pay less.

128805.q: Who helps to pay for public hospitals?
128805.e: Hospitals are paid for by health insurance and by the canton. The canton uses tax money for this.
128805.m: The canton helps pay for hospitals.

128806.q: In the town park, flowers are planted and benches repaired. Who usually pays for that?
128806.e: Parks belong to everyone. That is why the municipality pays for their upkeep with tax money.
128806.m: The park is there for everyone.

128807.q: A new bridge is being built over the river. Where does the money come from?
a: From the state, so from taxes
128807.e: Large structures like bridges are paid for by the municipality, canton or Confederation. The money comes from taxes.
128807.m: Bridges connect, and taxes pay for them.

128808.q: Who pays for buses and trains?
a: Passengers with tickets and the state with taxes
128808.e: Tickets don't cover all the costs. The rest is paid by the municipality, canton and Confederation with tax money.
128808.m: Tickets plus taxes: that's how the bus runs.

128809.q: Why is a bus ticket cheaper than what the journey really costs?
a: Because tax money pays part of it
Because the bus doesn't need fuel
128809.e: Buses and trains cost a lot. The state pays part with taxes so that everyone can travel cheaply.

128810.q: Who pays taxes on their wages?
128810.e: Anyone who works and gets a wage pays part of it as taxes. People who earn more pay more.
128810.m: If you earn a wage, you pay taxes.

a: Yes, companies pay taxes on their profits
128811.e: Not only people but companies pay taxes too. They pay on the money they have earned.

a: The village or town where you live
128812.e: The municipality is your village or your town. It looks after things near you, such as school and playgrounds.
128812.m: The municipality is very close to me.

128813.q: What do people mean when they talk about the “Confederation”?
128813.e: The “Confederation” means the state of the whole of Switzerland. It looks after things that are important for the whole country.
128813.m: The Confederation is the whole of Switzerland.

128814.q: In which city does the Swiss government work?
128814.e: The Swiss government, the Federal Council, works in Bern. Bern is the federal city.
128814.m: The Confederation is based in Bern.

128815.e: The municipality is in the canton, and all the cantons together make up the Confederation, that is Switzerland.
128815.m: Municipality, canton, Confederation: small, medium, large.

128816.e: The municipality is the smallest level. Several municipalities together make up a canton.
128816.m: The municipality is the smallest level.

128817.q: Who usually looks after the playground in your neighbourhood?
128817.e: The municipality looks after things that are close by. These include playgrounds and neighbourhood streets.
128817.m: What's close by is done by the municipality.

128818.q: Who pays for the motorways in Switzerland?
128818.e: Motorways are important for the whole country. That is why the Confederation looks after them.

128819.q: Who is responsible for the Swiss army?
128819.e: The army protects the whole country. That is why the Confederation pays for it with tax money.
128819.m: The army belongs to the Confederation.

128820.q: In Switzerland, who do the police usually belong to?
128820.e: Almost every canton has its own cantonal police. The canton pays for it with tax money.
128820.m: The police are usually paid for by the canton.

128822.q: What is the tax called that is included in the price of many things in a shop?
128822.e: VAT is already included in the price of many goods. The shop passes it on to the Confederation.
128822.m: VAT is included in the price.

128823.q: Where can you see how much VAT you have paid?
128823.e: The receipt often shows in small print how much VAT is included in the price. In Switzerland it is abbreviated MWST.

128824.q: Who does the shop pass the VAT money on to?
128824.e: The shop collects VAT when it sells things. Then it passes it on to the Confederation.
128824.m: The shop collects, the Confederation receives.

128826.q: Why do lots of people pay taxes together?
a: So that together they can pay for expensive things for everyone
So that nobody has to work any more
128826.e: One family alone can't pay for a school or a bridge. Together everyone can manage it.

128827.q: Could one family alone pay for a whole hospital?
a: No, that needs money from many people
128827.e: A hospital costs a great deal of money. Only if many people pay together is there enough.
128827.m: Many small contributions add up to a lot.

128828.q: In Switzerland, people who earn a lot pay ...
a: more taxes than someone with a low wage
taxes only once in their life
128828.e: People who earn more money can contribute more. That is why they pay more taxes. This is a fair way of sharing.
128828.m: Those who have more give more.

128829.q: Which statement about taxes is true?
a: Everyone helps so that everyone is well off
Only one person pays for everything
Taxes are only for the king
128829.e: With taxes everyone shares the costs of schools, roads and help. That way the whole community is better off.

128830.q: The class collects money for a trip: each child gives something. What is this like?
128830.e: With taxes, each person also gives a share, and something for everyone is paid for with it. Just like the class kitty.
128830.m: Taxes are like a big class kitty.

128831.q: Adults work and get a wage. What do they do with part of it?
a: They give it to the school
They have to give it to the bank
They pay the police directly with it
128831.e: Part of a wage goes as taxes to the municipality, canton and Confederation. Things for everyone are paid for with it.
128831.m: Part of your wage becomes tax.

128832.q: What is the office that collects taxes called?
128832.e: The tax office works out how much someone has to pay and collects the money.
128832.m: The tax office collects the taxes.

128833.q: Your parents are sitting at the table filling in papers about their wages. What are they probably doing?
128833.e: In the tax return, adults write down how much they have earned. Then it is worked out how much tax they pay.
128833.m: The tax return shows what you have earned.

128834.q: How often do adults in Switzerland normally fill in their tax return?
128834.e: The tax return is done once a year. You write down what you earned the previous year.

128835.q: Does a child with pocket money have to fill in a tax return?
128835.e: Children don't do their own tax return. Adults do that. But when shopping, children pay VAT too.

128836.q: Who usually makes sure that clean water comes out of the tap?
128836.e: The municipality looks after the water pipes. This is mainly paid for with charges for the water.
128836.m: Clean water thanks to the municipality.

128837.q: Who pays for the street lights that shine at night?
a: The people who go for walks at night
128837.e: Street lights make the way safe at night. They are usually paid for by the municipality with tax money.

128838.q: A zebra crossing in front of the school is being repainted. Who pays for this?
128838.e: Zebra crossings are part of the road. The municipality or canton pays for them with taxes.
128838.m: Safe routes to school cost money.

128839.q: In winter a snowplough clears the road. Who pays for the snowplough?
a: The municipality or canton, with taxes
128839.e: So that roads are safe in winter, the municipality and canton clear the snow. They pay for this with taxes.

128840.q: At state school, who often pays for the school books?
128840.e: At state school, children get many school books without having to buy them. This is paid for with tax money.
128840.m: School books are often paid for by taxes.

128841.q: The school gym is getting new mats. Where does the money usually come from?
a: From the children in the class
128841.e: The gym belongs to the school. The municipality pays for new equipment with taxes.

128842.q: Which number do you call if someone is badly injured?
128842.e: On 144 you reach the ambulance service. Emergency numbers are important for everyone.

128843.e: You can reach the police on 117. The police are paid for with tax money.

128844.q: What is the number of Rega, which helps by helicopter?
128844.e: Rega rescues people by helicopter. You can reach it on 1414.

128845.q: What do you get back for your taxes?
a: Things everyone uses, like schools and roads
128845.e: You don't get a present of your own for taxes. Instead there are schools, roads, police and much more for everyone.

128846.q: There is a public toilet in the park. Who usually pays for it?
128846.e: Many public toilets are built and cleaned by the municipality. The money often comes from taxes.

128847.q: Who helps to make sure that hiking trails are marked in yellow and kept in good condition?
128847.e: Hiking trails are looked after by cantons, municipalities and hiking associations. Part of the money comes from taxes.

128848.q: There are rubbish bins in the park. Who empties them?
128848.e: The municipality puts up rubbish bins and has them emptied. This is paid for partly with taxes.
128848.m: Rubbish in the bin, and the municipality collects it.

128849.q: What happens if lots of people throw rubbish on the ground?
a: The municipality has to pay more for clearing up
128849.e: Clearing up costs money, and that often comes from taxes. Anyone who disposes of rubbish properly helps everyone.
128849.m: Rubbish in the bin saves money for everyone.

128850.q: Why shouldn't you break anything in the park?
a: Everyone pays for the repair with their taxes
Because only adults are allowed there
Because the park belongs to the Confederation
128850.e: Benches and play equipment in the park are paid for with taxes. If they get broken, everyone pays for the repair.
128850.m: We protect what belongs to everyone.

128851.q: Who often provides the collection point for glass and aluminium?
128851.e: Many municipalities have collection points for glass, aluminium and paper. That way things can be recycled.
128851.m: Glass and aluminium go to the collection point.

128852.q: Ben says: “I never go to the swimming pool, so I don't need taxes.” What is true?
a: He still uses roads, school and more
He is right, he doesn't need anything
Taxes are only for swimming pools
He only has to pay dog tax
128852.e: Taxes pay for lots of different things. Even people who don't go swimming use schools, roads and hospitals.
128852.m: Everyone uses something that taxes pay for.

128853.q: Why is it fair that people with low wages pay less tax?
a: They need their money for food and housing
128853.e: People who earn little need most of their money for the essentials. That is why they pay less tax.
128853.m: Everyone gives as much as they can.

128854.q: What is the difference between a fine and a tax?
a: A fine is a punishment, a tax is not
A tax is always a punishment
128854.e: You pay a fine if you have done something forbidden, for example parked in the wrong place. You pay taxes quite normally for shared tasks.
128854.m: A fine is a punishment, a tax is a contribution.

128856.q: What are the boxes with little bags for dog poo by the path for?
a: So that dog owners can dispose of the poo cleanly
128856.e: The municipality puts up these boxes so that paths stay clean. This is often paid for with the dog tax.
128856.m: Dog poo goes in the bag, then in the bin.

128857.e: In Switzerland there are three levels: the municipality, the canton and the Confederation. All three receive taxes.
128857.m: Taxes go to the municipality, canton and Confederation.

128858.q: In many small municipalities, where can adults have a say in what money is spent on?
128858.e: In many municipalities the voters meet at the municipal assembly. There they decide, for example, on a new school building.
128858.m: At the municipal assembly everyone has a say.

128859.q: In Switzerland, adults can often vote on things. What, for example?
a: Whether the municipality builds a new swimming pool
128859.e: In Switzerland the voters often decide for themselves what tax money is spent on.
128859.m: In Switzerland lots of people have a say.

128860.q: The municipality plans how much money it will spend next year. What is this plan called?
128860.e: A budget is a plan for money. It shows how much money the municipality takes in and spends.

128861.q: What is sensible when a municipality spends tax money?
a: It spends it carefully on important things
It spends it all in one day
It only buys the most expensive things
It saves everything and builds nothing
128861.e: Tax money is everyone's money. That is why the municipality should plan well and spend it carefully.
128861.m: Tax money is spent with care.

128862.q: Who pays the teacher at a state nursery school?
128862.e: The state nursery school (Kindergarten) is part of the state school system. The teacher is paid with tax money.
128862.m: Nursery school is paid for with taxes too.

128863.q: In many municipalities, children have school dental check-ups. Who often helps to pay for this?
128863.e: Many municipalities organise dental check-ups for schoolchildren and pay part of the cost.
128863.m: Healthy teeth, thanks partly to the municipality.

128864.q: Many museums get money from the canton or the city. Where does this money come from?
128864.e: Museums show art and history for everyone. Municipalities and cantons often support them with tax money.

128865.q: A fallen tree is lying across the forest path. Who often clears it away?
a: The forestry service of the municipality or canton
128865.e: The forestry service looks after the forest and forest paths. It is partly paid for with tax money.
128865.m: The forest is looked after too.

128866.q: A new cycle path is being built. Who usually pays for it?
a: The cyclists when they set off
128866.e: Cycle paths are part of the roads. The municipality or canton builds them with tax money.

128867.q: Who helps to pay for new railway lines in Switzerland?
128867.e: Railway lines are important for the whole country. The Confederation pays a lot towards them, including with tax money.
128867.m: The Confederation helps with the railway.

128868.q: What would be difficult without taxes?
a: Having a school for all children
128868.e: Without taxes, many families could not afford school. Taxes make sure that all children can learn.
128868.m: Taxes make school possible for everyone.

128869.q: Which of these things is NOT paid for with tax money?
a: The road in front of your house
128869.e: Your family or you buy your own toys. School, the fire brigade and roads are paid for with taxes.
128869.m: What belongs to you, you pay for yourself.

128870.q: What does your family buy itself and not with taxes?
128870.e: The family buys food for home itself. Public things like school are paid for with taxes.
128870.m: The family pays for the morning snack.

128871.q: What does “public” mean, for example in a public playground?
128871.e: Public things are there for everyone. They are often paid for with taxes.

128872.q: Deductions are taken from wages every month. What for, for example?
128872.e: Contributions are taken from wages, for example for the AHV. Most people pay their taxes later with a bill from the tax office.
128872.m: You don't keep all of your wage.

128873.q: How do adults find out how much tax they have to pay?
a: They get a bill from the tax office
They pay as much as they like
They read it in the newspaper
128873.e: After the tax return, the tax office works out how much someone has to pay and sends a bill.
128873.m: The tax office sends the bill.

128874.q: Does how much tax you pay depend on where you live?
a: Yes, depending on the municipality and canton
No, it's exactly the same everywhere
128874.e: In Switzerland the cantons and municipalities help decide how high taxes are. That is why they are not the same everywhere.
128874.m: Where you live changes your taxes.

128875.q: What does the municipality do with its taxes, for example?
a: It builds and looks after the school building
128875.e: With taxes, the municipality pays for things for everyone nearby, such as the school building, playgrounds and local roads.

128876.q: Nora breaks her arm and goes to hospital. Who pays for the treatment?
a: Health insurance and the canton together
128876.e: Health insurance pays a large part. For a stay in hospital, the canton also pays with tax money.
128876.m: Health insurance and taxes help in hospital.

128877.q: A baker sells lots of croissants and earns money. What does the bakery have to do?
a: Only bake bread from now on
128877.e: Companies that make a profit pay taxes on it. This includes small shops like bakeries.

a: The money left over after all costs
The money in the till in the morning
128878.e: Profit is what a company has earned after taking away all costs. The company pays taxes on the profit.
128878.m: Profit is what is left over.

128879.q: Do you pay VAT when you buy a comic in a shop?
a: Yes, it is included in the price
128879.e: VAT is also included in the price of books and comics. A lower rate applies to books.
128879.m: There is VAT in a comic too.

128880.q: The price tag says 2 francs. Do you have to pay extra tax at the till?
a: No, the tax is already in the price
128880.e: In Switzerland, VAT is already included in the price shown. You simply pay the price on the tag.
128880.m: The price on the tag is what you pay.

128881.e: VAT is included in the price. That is why everyone who shops pays it, including children.
128881.m: If you shop, you pay VAT.

128882.q: What is the Confederation responsible for?
a: For things that affect the whole country
128882.e: The Confederation looks after big tasks for the whole of Switzerland, such as motorways and the army.
128882.m: The Confederation looks after the whole country.

128883.q: Which canton is the city of Lugano in?
128883.e: Lugano is in the south of Switzerland in the canton of Ticino. Italian is spoken there.

128884.q: In many cantons, who is responsible for the grammar schools (Gymnasien)?
128884.e: Grammar schools and cantonal schools usually belong to the canton. It pays for them with tax money.
128884.m: The canton pays for cantonal schools.

128885.q: Why have taxes existed for a very long time?
a: There have always been shared tasks
Because there used to be no shops
Because people used to be richer
Because there used to be no roads
128885.e: Even a very long time ago, people pooled their resources, for example for paths and protection. Today this is called taxes.
128885.m: Paying together is an old idea.

128886.q: Which rule is the fairest for sharing the costs of things for everyone?
a: Everyone gives something, and those who have more give more
Only the smallest pay for everything
Only one person pays for everything
128886.e: Taxes follow this idea: everyone helps, but those who earn more contribute more.
128886.m: Fair means: according to what you can afford.

128887.q: What about someone who deliberately doesn't pay taxes even though they should?
a: That is forbidden and unfair to everyone
128887.e: Anyone who has to pay taxes and deliberately doesn't is doing something forbidden. Then the others have to carry more.

128888.q: The school playground is getting a new climbing frame. Where does the money usually come from?
a: From the municipality, so from taxes
From the parents of the class
128888.e: Playgrounds belong to the school. The municipality pays for new play equipment with taxes.

128889.q: What happens to the dirty water from the shower and toilet?
a: It is cleaned at the sewage treatment plant
It flows straight into the lake
It stays in a tank in the cellar
128889.e: The waste water flows to a sewage treatment plant and is cleaned there. Municipalities build and run these plants.
128889.m: The sewage treatment plant cleans the water.

128890.q: Which task is mainly paid for by the Confederation?
128890.e: National defence is the job of the Confederation. It pays for the army with federal money, for example from the direct federal tax and VAT.
128890.m: The army? The Confederation pays for that.

128891.q: Who usually pays for the fire brigade in your village?
128891.e: In Switzerland the fire brigade is usually the job of the municipality. It is paid for with municipal taxes and fire service charges.
128891.m: The local fire brigade belongs to the municipality.

128892.q: Which task belongs mainly to the canton in Switzerland?
128892.e: The police are mostly the job of the cantons. That is why there is, for example, the Bern Cantonal Police or the Zurich Cantonal Police.

128893.q: Why are there taxes at three levels in Switzerland?
a: The Confederation, cantons and municipalities each have their own tasks
Because there are three national languages
So that you pay three times as much
128893.e: The Confederation, cantons and municipalities carry out different tasks. Each level needs its own money for this and is therefore allowed to collect taxes.
128893.m: Three levels, three areas of responsibility.

128894.q: Who is responsible for the motorways in Switzerland?
128894.e: Since 2008 the national roads, that is the motorways, have belonged to the Confederation. It builds and maintains them.

128895.q: Who mainly pays for state schools in Switzerland?
128895.e: Compulsory schooling is the job of the cantons and municipalities. It is paid for with tax money, which is why it is free for children.
128895.m: State school is free because everyone pays taxes.

128896.q: Who pays for the two federal institutes of technology in Zurich and Lausanne?
128896.e: ETH Zurich and EPFL in Lausanne are federal universities. They are mostly funded with federal money.
128896.m: The ETH and EPFL are federal universities.

128897.q: Mia lives in Lucerne. Who does she pay income tax to?
a: To the Confederation, canton and municipality
Only to the city of Lucerne
128897.e: Income tax goes to all three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Usually it is all handled by the cantonal tax office.

128898.q: What does the municipality pay for with its taxes, among other things?
128898.e: Municipalities look after things nearby: nursery school, school buildings, local roads, waste water or playgrounds.
128898.m: Municipal money for what's on your doorstep.

128899.q: Who is mainly responsible for hospitals in Switzerland?
128899.e: Health care with hospitals is mainly the job of the cantons. They pay part of the hospital costs with tax money.

a: A percentage by which the basic tax is multiplied
The length of the tax form
A discount for families with children
The signature on the tax return
128900.e: Many cantons first calculate a basic tax. The tax multiplier of the canton and municipality then decides how much you pay in the end.
128900.m: The tax multiplier makes the tax bigger or smaller.

128901.q: The basic tax is 1,000 francs and the municipal tax multiplier is 120%. How much is the municipal tax?
128901.e: 120 per cent of 1,000 francs is 1,200 francs. The tax multiplier is multiplied by the basic tax.

128902.q: The municipality lowers its tax multiplier from 100% to 90%. What does this mean?
a: Everyone pays the same as before
128902.e: A lower tax multiplier means less municipal tax. Federal tax and VAT are not affected.
128902.m: Lower tax multiplier, lower municipal tax.

128903.q: Who decides on the tax multiplier in a municipality?
a: The voters or the municipal parliament
128903.e: The municipal tax multiplier is set by the municipal assembly or the municipal parliament, often together with the budget. Sometimes the people vote on it at the ballot box.
128903.m: The village sets its own tax multiplier.

128904.q: Two municipalities in the same canton have different tax multipliers. What follows from this?
a: With the same income you don't pay the same amount
You pay exactly the same in both
128904.e: Because each municipality sets its own tax multiplier, you may pay more or less tax in the next village with the same wage.
128904.m: Same wage, different village, different tax.

128905.q: Why does a municipality sometimes raise its tax multiplier?
a: Because it needs more money for its tasks
Because the residents think it's funny
Because the Confederation orders it every year
128905.e: If a municipality builds a new school, for example, or has higher costs, it can raise more income with a higher tax multiplier.

128906.q: A T-shirt costs 100 francs without VAT. How much does it cost with 8.1% VAT?
128906.e: 8.1 per cent of 100 francs is 8.10 francs. Together that makes 108.10 francs.

128907.q: Which VAT rate has applied to food since 2024?
128907.e: The reduced rate of 2.6 per cent applies to everyday necessities such as food, books and medicines.

128908.q: A lower VAT rate applies to hotel stays in Switzerland. Why?
a: Because hotels belong to the Confederation
Because overnight stays count as food
128908.e: A special rate of 3.8 per cent applies to overnight stays with breakfast in hotels and holiday flats. It is meant to strengthen tourism.
128908.m: Hotel nights are taxed less, which helps tourism.

128909.q: Who hands VAT over to the state?
a: Each customer directly at the bank counter
128909.e: Customers pay VAT in the price. Shops collect it and transfer it to the Federal Tax Administration.
128909.m: Customers pay, companies hand it over.

128910.q: Which level of government receives VAT?
128910.e: VAT is a federal tax. It is one of the Confederation's most important sources of income.

128911.q: Why is VAT called an indirect tax?
a: You pay it through the price, not with a bill of its own
Because you never have to pay it
128911.e: With indirect taxes you don't get a tax bill. The tax is hidden in the price, and the seller passes it on.

128912.q: A small shop sells less than 100,000 francs' worth of goods a year. What applies?
a: It doesn't have to account for VAT
It pays twice as much VAT
It isn't allowed to sell anything
It pays dog tax instead of VAT
128912.e: Companies with an annual turnover of less than 100,000 francs are exempt from VAT. This takes the burden off very small businesses.
128912.m: Turnover under 100,000 francs: no VAT obligation.

128913.q: Which statement about VAT is true?
a: Part of it helps to fund the AHV (old-age insurance)
It is only charged at Christmas
128913.e: The voters decided that part of VAT goes to the AHV. In this way it helps to secure pensions.

128914.q: How can the standard VAT rate be raised?
128914.e: The maximum VAT rates are in the Federal Constitution. To raise them you therefore need the approval of the people and the cantons.
128914.m: Higher VAT only if the people say yes.

128915.q: A book costs 20 francs. Which VAT rate is included in it?
128915.e: Books, newspapers and magazines fall under the reduced rate of 2.6 per cent, just like food.

128916.q: What do you pay income tax on?
a: On the size of your flat
128916.e: Income tax is calculated according to income, mainly wages, but also pensions or interest.

128917.q: Which tax is a direct tax?
128917.e: Direct taxes are collected directly from the person, with a bill of their own. Income tax is the most important example.
128917.m: Direct tax: your own bill from the tax office.

128918.q: Which document does Mr Meier get from his employer for his tax return?
128918.e: Every year the employer issues a salary certificate. It shows how much you have earned. It goes with the tax return.
128918.m: The salary certificate shows your annual wage.

128919.q: What does a deduction mean in a tax return?
a: An amount that reduces your taxable income
A cash present from the state
128919.e: Certain costs, for example for travelling to work, may be deducted from your income. Then the tax is calculated on a smaller amount.
128919.m: Deductions make your taxable income smaller.

a: The money in your savings account
128920.e: You take the permitted deductions away from your total income. What is left is your taxable income. The tax is calculated on that.
128920.m: Income minus deductions equals taxable income.

128921.q: Which costs can you often deduct in your tax return?
128921.e: People who commute to work may deduct their travel costs within certain limits. You can't deduct holidays or presents.
128921.m: Travel to work yes, holidays no.

128922.q: Does a child have to pay income tax on their pocket money?
a: No, pocket money is not taxable income
Yes, but only in the canton of Bern
Only if it is more than 5 francs
128922.e: Pocket money is a gift from parents and not a wage. You don't have to pay income tax on it.

128923.q: For what period is income tax usually calculated?
128923.e: In Switzerland the tax period is the calendar year from January to December. You fill in the tax return for it the following year.
128923.m: Earn in one year, declare it the next.

128924.q: What is wealth tax charged on?
a: On savings and property such as securities or a house
On every purchase in a shop
128924.e: Wealth tax is calculated on assets, for example money in accounts, shares or property, minus debts.

128925.q: Which date often counts for wealth in the tax return?
128925.e: For wealth tax, what usually counts is the amount at the end of the tax period, that is on 31 December.
128925.m: Wealth counts at the end of the year.

128926.q: How do debts affect wealth tax?
a: You have to give them to the state
128926.e: For wealth tax, net wealth is what counts. Debts, such as a mortgage, are deducted from wealth.
128926.m: Wealth minus debts equals net wealth.

128927.q: Luca is 12 and has 2,000 francs in his savings account. Who declares this in a tax return?
a: His parents, in their tax return
Luca, in his own tax return
128927.e: The wealth of children under 18 is listed in their parents' tax return. They don't need their own return for it.
128927.m: A child's savings account goes in the parents' tax return.

128928.q: What is a tax-free allowance in wealth tax?
a: An amount up to which wealth is not taxed
A penalty for saving too much
128928.e: The cantons have tax-free allowances. That is why people with only a little wealth don't pay wealth tax.

128929.q: The Keller family gets a dog. Where do they usually have to register it so the dog tax can be calculated?
128929.e: Dogs usually have to be registered with the municipality where you live. It then sends the bill for the dog tax every year.
128929.m: Register your dog with the municipality.

128930.q: How often is dog tax usually paid?
128930.e: Dog tax is an annual tax. Anyone who has a dog on the reference date gets the bill.

128931.q: For which pet is there a special tax in many municipalities?
128931.e: Only dogs are taxed in Switzerland. You don't pay tax for cats, fish or guinea pigs.

a: A tax on tickets for events
A tax on SBB train tickets
128932.e: Some municipalities or cantons charge an entertainment tax on admission, for example to the cinema, concerts or sports events. Many have abolished it.
128932.m: Entertainment tax is included in the ticket price.

128933.q: Noah buys a concert ticket in a city with an entertainment tax. How does he pay it?
a: It is usually included in the ticket price
He has to work it out himself
128933.e: The organisers add the entertainment tax to the price and hand it over to the municipality. So Noah pays it with the ticket.
128933.m: You pay entertainment tax with the ticket.

128934.q: Where does the money from tobacco tax go?
a: Mainly to the AHV and IV (old-age and disability insurance)
128934.e: Tobacco tax is a federal tax. Its revenue is used for the AHV and the IV.

128935.q: Why do cigarettes have a special tax?
a: It brings in money and is meant to reduce smoking
Because they come from the sea
Because they used to be free
128935.e: Tobacco tax makes cigarettes more expensive. This brings the state money and can help to reduce smoking.

128936.q: On which drink does the Confederation charge a particularly high alcohol tax?
128936.e: Distilled drinks like schnapps, vodka or whisky are taxed by the Confederation. This spirits tax is much higher than the beer tax.

128937.q: Part of the tax on spirits goes to the cantons. What must they use this money for?
a: To fight alcohol abuse and addiction
128937.e: Ten per cent of the revenue from the spirits tax goes to the cantons. They must use the money to fight alcohol abuse and addiction.
128937.m: Money from the spirits tax helps fight addiction.

128938.q: Which tax do breweries in Switzerland pay to the Confederation?
128938.e: The Confederation charges its own beer tax on beer. It is included in the price of every beer.

128939.q: Which alcoholic drink is exempt from a special alcohol tax in Switzerland?
128939.e: In Switzerland there is no special excise duty on wine. Beer and spirits, on the other hand, are specially taxed. VAT still applies.
128939.m: Wine: no alcohol tax of its own.

128940.q: What is fuel tax charged on?
128940.e: Fuel tax (mineral oil tax) is a federal tax on fuels such as petrol and diesel. It is included in every litre at the petrol station.
128940.m: Filling up means paying fuel tax.

128941.q: What is a large part of fuel tax used for?
128941.e: An important part of fuel tax goes into building and maintaining roads and into transport.
128941.m: Those who drive on the roads pay for the roads.

128942.q: Mr Rossi fills up with 40 litres of petrol. Which taxes are included in the price?
128942.e: The petrol price includes fuel tax and VAT on top. That is why the state makes up a large part of the price.
128942.m: There are two taxes in petrol.

128943.q: Which authority is responsible for customs in Switzerland?
a: The Federal Office for Customs and Border Security
128943.e: The Federal Office for Customs and Border Security, or FOCBS for short, checks goods at the border and collects customs duties and charges.

128944.q: What has applied since 2024 to industrial goods such as bikes or clothes when they are imported?
a: They can no longer be imported
128944.e: Since 1 January 2024, Switzerland no longer charges customs duties on industrial products. But VAT on imports still applies.
128944.m: Industrial tariffs have been gone since 2024.

128945.q: Why are there still customs duties on many farm products such as meat?
a: Because meat from abroad is banned
So that farmers pay more taxes
128945.e: Customs duties make imported farm products more expensive. That way Swiss farms can compete better with cheaper goods from abroad.

128946.q: Sara orders clothes from a foreign online shop. What can be charged when they are imported?
a: VAT and a customs clearance fee
128946.e: Swiss VAT is also charged on orders from abroad. On top of that there may be a fee from the parcel service for customs clearance.
128946.m: Parcel from abroad: VAT may be added.

128947.q: How much does the motorway vignette for a car cost?
128947.e: The motorway vignette costs 40 francs. It is valid for the whole year and must be bought to use the motorways.

a: An electronic vignette linked to the number plate
A vignette only for electric cars
An email from the tax office
128948.e: Since 2023 you can also buy the vignette electronically. It is then linked to the number plate instead of being a sticker on the windscreen.
128948.m: The e-vignette is linked to the number plate.

128949.q: Until when is a year's vignette valid?
a: Until 31 January of the following year
128949.e: A vignette is valid from 1 December of the previous year until 31 January of the following year, so 14 months.
128949.m: The vignette is valid until the end of the January after.

a: Anyone driving a car or motorbike on the motorway
128950.e: Cars and motorbikes up to 3.5 tonnes need a vignette for motorways. Heavy lorries pay the HVF instead.
128950.m: Drive on the motorway, have a vignette.

128951.q: What is the money from the motorway vignette used for?
128951.e: The vignette is the national road charge. You pay it for using the motorways, and the money is meant for the national roads.

128952.q: What do heavy lorries pay instead of the vignette?
128952.e: Lorries over 3.5 tonnes pay the HVF (LSVA). It depends on the kilometres driven, the weight and the pollutant emissions.

128953.q: What is the situation with a bike vignette in Switzerland today?
a: It is only compulsory for children
It is also valid for the motorway
128953.e: The bike vignette was abolished in 2012. Damage caused by bikes is now usually covered by private liability insurance.
128953.m: The bike vignette no longer exists.

128954.q: What is the difference between a fee and a tax?
a: For a fee you get a specific service
A fee is always more expensive
You never have to pay taxes
128954.e: You pay a fee for a specific service, such as a passport. You pay taxes without getting something directly in return, for the tasks of the state.

128955.q: Which example is a fee and not a tax?
a: The price of a new passport
128955.e: Anyone who orders a passport pays a fee for it. You get a specific service: the identity document.
128955.m: Ordering a passport costs a fee.

128956.q: The Huber family buys official rubbish bags from the municipality. What are they paying for?
128956.e: In many municipalities the price of rubbish bags includes a fee. People who produce more rubbish pay more. This is called the polluter pays principle.
128956.m: Those who make more rubbish pay more.

128957.q: What does the polluter pays principle mean for fees?
a: Whoever needs a service pays for it
128957.e: With the polluter pays principle, the person who causes the costs pays. Examples are the bag charge or the water charge.

128958.q: Tim parks the car in town and pays at the machine. What is that?
128958.e: The town charges a fee for parking on public land. You pay for using the parking space.
128958.m: Use a parking space, pay a fee.

a: A charge on guests' overnight stays in holiday resorts
A tax on treatments at the doctor's
128959.e: Holiday resorts charge guests a tourist tax per night. It pays for things like hiking trails or activities for tourists.
128959.m: Holiday guests pay the tourist tax.

128960.q: Which area does the Confederation spend the most money on?
a: Social welfare, such as the AHV
128960.e: The Confederation's biggest item of spending is social welfare, mainly contributions to the AHV and other social insurance schemes. The army, education and transport also cost a lot, but less.
128960.m: Most federal money goes on social security.

128961.q: Which area is paid for with tax money?
128961.e: Education and research are among the big expenses of the Confederation, cantons and municipalities. These include schools and universities.

128962.q: What does the state pay for with taxes that benefits everyone?
128962.e: Transport routes such as roads and railway lines are built with taxes and charges. They are available to everyone.

128963.q: Which of these expenses does the state not pay for with tax money?
128963.e: Taxes fund shared tasks. Everyone has to pay for private things like their own clothes themselves.
128963.m: Taxes for shared things, not private ones.

128964.q: Why does a bus ticket cost less than the journey really costs?
a: The Confederation, cantons and municipalities add tax money
Because the bus runs for free
Because the drivers don't get paid
128964.e: Many bus and train lines don't cover their costs with tickets alone. The public sector pays part of it with tax money.

128965.q: What does tax competition between cantons mean?
a: Cantons try to attract companies and people with low taxes
Cantons play football against each other
All cantons have exactly the same taxes
The Confederation hands out tax prizes
128965.e: Because the cantons largely set their own taxes, they compete with each other. Low taxes can attract companies and residents.

128966.q: Which canton is known for particularly low taxes?
128966.e: The canton of Zug has had comparatively low taxes for decades. That is why many companies have their headquarters there.
128966.m: Zug is known for low taxes.

128967.q: What can be a disadvantage of very low taxes?
a: The canton has less money for its tasks
There are no more roads in the country
128967.e: Low taxes do attract companies, but they bring in less income per person. The canton then has to manage its money carefully.
128967.m: Low taxes also mean less income.

128968.q: Which tax is the same in all cantons?
128968.e: VAT is a federal tax and is the same everywhere in Switzerland. Cantonal, municipal and dog taxes differ from place to place.

128969.q: Where can you fill in your tax return in many cantons today?
a: Online, with software from the canton
Only at the railway ticket office
128969.e: Most cantons offer tax software or an online portal. But you can often still hand in a paper form.
128969.m: You can also do your tax return online.

128970.q: By when does the tax return have to be handed in in many cantons?
a: By the end of March of the following year
128970.e: In many cantons the deadline is the end of March. Anyone who needs more time can usually ask for an extension.
128970.m: Tax return: often by the end of March.

128971.q: What can you do if you can't manage your tax return on time?
128971.e: You can usually ask the tax office for an extension. Anyone who hands in nothing at all gets a reminder and risks a fine.
128971.m: Too late? Ask for an extension.

128972.q: What does the tax office do after the tax return has been handed in?
a: It checks it and calculates the taxes
128972.e: The tax office checks the details and draws up the tax assessment. This states how much tax you owe.

128973.q: Why should you keep documents such as receipts?
a: To prove deductions in your tax return
Because the shop wants them back
128973.e: For many deductions, for example further training costs, the tax office needs proof. That is why it is worth keeping receipts in order.

128974.q: What happens if someone deliberately hides income in their tax return?
a: They have to pay the tax afterwards and get a fine
128974.e: Anyone who deliberately does not declare income or wealth is committing tax evasion. If it is discovered, they have to pay the back taxes and a fine.

128975.q: Why do you often get a provisional tax bill during the current year?
a: So that you can spread out paying your taxes
Because you have to pay twice
Because the tax office gives money away
Because the tax return has been abolished
128975.e: Many cantons send a provisional bill based on an estimate. It is settled later with the final bill.

128976.q: Elias is 19, at university and has no income. Does he have to fill in a tax return?
a: Yes, he has to hand it in even without income
Only if he has a car
128976.e: All adults living in Switzerland have to hand in a tax return, even if they have little or no income.
128976.m: Being an adult means handing in a tax return.

128977.q: What do apprentices get from their employer that they need for their tax return?
128977.e: Apprentices also get a salary certificate. It shows their apprentice wage for the year, which goes in the tax return.
128977.m: There is a salary certificate for apprentices too.

128978.q: Who can help young adults with their first tax return?
a: Parents, or the tax office with advice
128978.e: Many tax offices offer information sheets and advice. Parents or advice centres are also happy to help the first time.
128978.m: If you have questions, the tax office can help.

128979.q: Which tax do car owners pay to the canton every year?
128979.e: Anyone with a registered car or motorbike pays the cantonal motor vehicle tax every year. It differs from canton to canton.
128979.m: Registered car, tax to the canton.

128980.q: Which tax do companies pay on their profit?
128980.e: Businesses such as public limited companies pay a profit tax on their profit to the Confederation, canton and municipality.

128981.q: Who levies inheritance taxes in Switzerland?
128981.e: Inheritance and gift taxes are a matter for the cantons. There is no federal tax on inheritances.
128981.m: Inheritance tax is a cantonal matter.

128982.q: Which federal authority deals with VAT?
128982.e: The Federal Tax Administration, or FTA for short, is responsible for VAT and the direct federal tax, among other things.

128983.q: What do Swiss men pay if they don't do military or civilian service?
128983.e: Men who are required to serve but don't do their service pay a substitute charge. It depends on their income.
128983.m: No service, then the exemption tax.

128984.q: Who must agree so that the Confederation can continue to levy VAT and the direct federal tax?
a: The people and the cantons in a vote
128984.e: The Federal Constitution only allows the Confederation these two taxes for a limited time. To extend them, the people and the cantons vote.
128984.m: Federal taxes regularly need the people's yes.

129075.q: What does a farmer do on the farm?
a: Looks after animals and grows plants
Drives a train across the country
129075.e: Farmers look after cows, pigs or chickens and grow grain, potatoes or vegetables.
129075.m: A lot of our food comes from farms.

129076.q: Which vehicle does a farmer often need in the field?
129076.e: With the tractor the farmer pulls trailers, a plough or a mower. This makes work in the fields much easier.
129076.m: The tractor is the favourite vehicle on the farm.

129077.q: Which material does a joiner work with most?
129077.e: Joiners make furniture such as tables, cupboards or beds out of wood. They also make doors and kitchens.
129077.m: The joiner turns wood into furniture.

129078.q: Who needs a plane to make wood smooth?
129078.e: With the plane, the joiner takes thin shavings off the wood. This makes the wood nice and smooth and straight.

129079.q: Which tools does a hairdresser need every day?
a: A brush and a paint roller
129079.e: The hairdresser cuts hair with scissors and a comb. She often needs a hairdryer too.
129079.m: Scissors and a comb belong in a hair salon.

129080.e: A hair salon has mirrors, chairs and washbasins. That is where hairdressers wash, cut and style hair.
129080.m: The hairdresser works in a salon.

129081.q: What does a train driver do?
129081.e: The train driver sits at the front in the driver's cab and brings the train safely and on time to its destination.
129081.m: The train driver drives the train.

129082.q: Where does the train driver sit during the journey?
a: Right at the front in the driver's cab
On the roof of the train
In the last carriage with the suitcases
129082.e: The driver's cab is at the front of the train. From there the driver can see the tracks and the signals.
129082.m: The train driver sits at the front of the train.

129083.q: What does a nurse do in hospital?
129083.e: Nurses take temperatures, give medicines and help patients in everyday life.
129083.m: Nurses help sick people get well.

129085.q: Where does a polymechanic usually work?
129085.e: In the workshop there are big machines for working metal. That is where the polymechanic works.

129086.q: What does a cook do in a restaurant?
129086.e: The cook chops, fries and cooks in the restaurant kitchen. Then the food is served to the guests.
129086.m: The cook cooks for lots of guests.

129087.q: Why do cooks often wear a white hat?
a: So that no hair falls into the food
So that they don't get cold
So that you can see them from far away
So that the sun doesn't dazzle them
129087.e: The tall white chef's hat keeps the hair together. That way no hair falls into the food.
129087.m: The chef's hat protects food from hair.

129089.q: Why should only experts work on cables and sockets?
a: Electricity can give you a serious shock
129089.e: An electric shock can seriously injure people. That is why only trained electricians work on cables and sockets.

129091.q: Which tool does a gardener use to give plants water?
129091.e: Plants get water from the watering can or the hose. Without water they would wilt.
129091.m: Plants need water from the watering can.

129092.q: Who helps when your dog is ill?
129092.e: The vet examines and treats sick animals. She also vaccinates dogs and cats.
129092.m: Sick animals go to the vet.

129093.q: Mia is taking her cat to be vaccinated. Where does she go?
129093.e: At the vet's surgery, animals are examined, vaccinated and treated.

129094.q: What is one of the jobs of police officers?
a: They keep people safe and maintain order
They bake bread for the village
They plant trees in the forest
129094.e: The police help at accidents, direct traffic and make sure everyone sticks to the rules.

129095.q: What does the fire brigade do besides putting out fires?
a: It also helps with accidents and floods
129095.e: The fire brigade rescues people and animals and helps with accidents, floods and storm damage.
129095.m: The fire brigade helps in many emergencies.

129096.e: Pilots fly planes or helicopters and bring passengers safely to their destination.
129096.m: The pilot flies high in the sky.

129097.q: What is the place where the pilot sits in the plane called?
129097.e: The cockpit is right at the front of the plane. It has lots of buttons, screens and the controls.
129097.m: The plane is flown from the cockpit.

129098.e: Postmen and postwomen deliver the post to people's letterboxes.

129100.q: What does a teacher do at school?
129100.e: Teachers explain reading, writing, maths and much more. They help children learn.

129101.q: What does the teacher often write on in the classroom?
129101.e: On the board or a big screen, the teacher shows what the class is learning.
129101.m: The board is the class's big exercise book.

129102.q: What does an IT specialist mainly work with?
129102.e: IT specialists write programs, set up computers and help when something doesn't work.
129102.m: The IT specialist speaks the language of computers.

129103.q: Who writes the programs for games and apps?
129103.e: Every game and every app is a program. IT specialists write the commands for the computer.
129103.m: Behind every app there is a program.

a: Walls out of bricks and concrete
129104.e: On the building site, bricklayers build walls out of bricks and concrete.
129104.m: The bricklayer builds brick by brick.

129105.q: Which tool does a bricklayer need for the mortar?
129105.e: With the trowel, the bricklayer spreads mortar between the bricks. That way they hold together firmly.

129106.q: Where does a bricklayer usually work?
129106.e: New houses go up on building sites. Bricklayers work there together with many other tradespeople.
129106.m: On the building site, a house grows.

129107.q: Why do people on a building site wear a helmet?
129107.e: Things can fall down on a building site. The helmet protects the head from injuries.

129108.q: Why does a baker often get up very early?
a: So that the bread is fresh in the morning
Because the bakery is closed in the evening
Because dough only rises at night
129108.e: Many people want fresh bread for breakfast. That is why bakers often start in the middle of the night or early in the morning.
129108.m: Getting up early brings fresh bread.

129109.q: Where is the bread baked in a bakery?
129109.e: In the hot oven, dough turns into crusty bread.
129109.m: The oven makes the bread crusty.

129111.q: Where do you pay for your shopping in a shop?
129111.e: At the till the goods are scanned, and you pay with cash or a card.

129112.q: What does a carpenter build out of wood?
129112.e: Carpenters build large wooden structures, for example the frame of a roof or whole wooden houses.
129112.m: The carpenter builds the roof out of wood.

129113.q: What is the difference between a joiner and a carpenter?
a: The carpenter builds large wooden structures, the joiner makes furniture
The joiner only works with metal
There is no difference at all
129113.e: Both work with wood. The carpenter builds roofs and wooden houses, the joiner makes furniture, doors and kitchens.

129114.q: Who do you call when water is dripping from the pipe?
129114.e: Plumbers lay water pipes and fit washbasins, toilets and showers.
129114.m: If it drips, the plumber helps.

129115.q: Who needs a pipe wrench for work?
129115.e: With the pipe wrench, the plumber tightens or loosens pipes and nuts.

129116.q: What does a painter do on a building site?
129116.e: Painters paint walls, outside walls, windows and doors. This makes a house look nice and protects it.
129116.m: The painter brings colour into the house.

129117.q: Which tool does a painter need for big walls?
129117.e: With a paint roller, the painter can paint large areas quickly and evenly.

129118.q: What does a mechanic do in the garage?
129118.e: In the garage the mechanic changes tyres and oil, for example, and repairs whatever is broken on the car.
129118.m: In the garage, the car gets fit again.

129119.q: Which tool does a mechanic often need?
129119.e: With a spanner, the mechanic tightens or loosens screws and nuts.

129120.e: Foresters look after the forest. They decide which trees are cut down and where new ones are planted.
129120.m: The forester looks after the forest.

129121.q: Who cuts down trees in the forest with a chainsaw?
129121.e: Forestry workers work in the forest. They cut down trees, plant young trees and look after forest paths.
129121.m: Foresters and forestry workers work in the forest.

129122.e: At the dentist your teeth are checked. If a tooth has a hole, the dentist fixes it with a filling.
129122.m: The dentist keeps your teeth healthy.

129123.q: Why do schoolchildren go for regular dental check-ups?
a: So that holes are found early
So that you never have to brush again
129123.e: At a check-up, small holes are spotted early. Then fixing them is easier and hurts less.

a: Hands out medicines and gives advice on them
129124.e: You get medicines at the chemist. The pharmacist explains how to take them properly.
129124.m: At the chemist you get advice and medicine.

129125.q: What does a bus driver do?
129125.e: Bus drivers follow a timetable from stop to stop and take people where they want to go.
129125.m: The bus driver takes you to the stop.

129126.q: How does the bus driver know when to be where?
129126.e: The timetable shows when the bus leaves from each stop. The driver sticks to it.
129126.m: The timetable tells you when the bus comes.

a: A place where small children are looked after
129128.e: Kita is short for Kindertagesstätte, a day nursery. Children are looked after there while their parents work.
129128.m: A Kita is a day nursery.

129129.e: Butchers, today called meat specialists, prepare meat and also make sausages from it.

129130.q: What does a dressmaker, officially a clothing designer, do?
129130.e: Clothing designers sew clothes and alter them, for example when a pair of trousers is too long.
129130.m: Clothes are made with a needle and thread.

129131.q: Who needs a sewing machine for work?
129131.e: With a sewing machine you can sew fabric much faster than by hand.

129132.q: Leo has a flat tyre on his bike. Who can help him?
129132.e: Bike mechanics, officially bicycle mechanics, fix tyres, brakes and chains.

129133.e: Florists work in a flower shop. They make bouquets and flower decorations for celebrations.
129133.m: The florist works magic with flowers.

129134.q: Who steers a ship on the lake?
129134.e: Passenger boats run on Swiss lakes. At the front, the captain steers the boat.
129134.m: On a ship, the captain is at the wheel.

129135.q: What does a zookeeper do at the zoo?
a: Feeds the animals and cleans the enclosures
Sells ice cream at the entrance
129135.e: Zookeepers make sure the zoo animals are well. They feed, clean and watch the animals.
129135.m: At the zoo, the zookeeper looks after the animals.

129136.q: Who comes in the ambulance when someone is injured?
129136.e: Paramedics give first aid and take injured people to hospital. Their number is 144.

129137.q: What is an apprenticeship, explained simply?
a: A way of learning a job after school
129137.e: In an apprenticeship you learn a job directly at a company and go to vocational school as well. Many young people in Switzerland do an apprenticeship.
129137.m: In an apprenticeship you learn a job.

129138.q: What do you call someone who is doing an apprenticeship?
129138.e: Someone doing an apprenticeship is called an apprentice. In Switzerland the official word today is “learner”.
129138.m: Someone doing an apprenticeship is an apprentice.

129139.q: Where does an apprentice learn most of their job?
129139.e: The training company is the firm where you do your apprenticeship. There a trainer shows you how the work is done.
129139.m: You learn the work at the training company.

129140.q: Where do apprentices go besides working at the company?
129140.e: At vocational school, apprentices learn the knowledge they need for their job, as well as general subjects.
129140.m: Work at the company, knowledge at vocational school.

129141.q: Do apprentices in Switzerland get paid for their work?
a: No, they have to pay themselves
129141.e: Apprentices work at the company and get an apprentice's wage every month. It goes up a little with each year of the apprenticeship.
129141.m: Apprentices already earn their own money.

129142.q: Nina wants to find out whether she would like being a cook. What can she do later on?
a: Try it out for a few days in a kitchen
Forget about the job straight away
129142.e: On a taster placement you work at a company for a few days. That way you see what the job is really like.
129142.m: A taster placement means trying out a job.

129143.q: When do young people in Switzerland usually do a taster placement?
a: At lower secondary school, aged about 13 to 15
129143.e: Choosing a career usually begins at lower secondary school. Then young people try out different jobs.
129143.m: Taster placements happen at lower secondary school.

129144.q: Lara is very good at drawing and making things. Which job would suit her well?
129144.e: Graphic designers design posters, books and logos. If you like drawing, you have a good strength for it.
129144.m: Your strengths show you jobs that suit you.

129145.q: Tim likes building things out of wood in his free time. Which job might he like?
129145.e: If you like building with wood, you might find a great job as a joiner or carpenter.
129145.m: A hobby can become a job.

129146.q: At home, Sara likes helping with the cooking best. Which job suits her?
129146.e: If you like cooking and trying out new recipes, you can become a cook.
129146.m: If you like cooking, you can become a cook.

129147.q: Jonas likes helping other people and is patient. Which job suits him?
129147.e: Nursing needs patience and enjoying helping others. Nurses look after sick and elderly people.
129147.m: Helping is fun, at work too.

129148.q: Elin likes taking old devices apart. Which job suits her?
129148.e: If you are curious about how machines work, you will enjoy technical jobs such as polymechanic or electronics technician.
129148.m: Curiosity about technology suits technical jobs.

129149.q: Ben likes being outside, even in the rain. Which job suits him?
129149.e: Forestry workers almost always work outside in the forest, in all weathers.
129149.m: If you like being outdoors, there are outdoor jobs.

129150.q: What does a forestry worker wear for protection when working with a chainsaw?
a: A helmet, ear protection and cut-resistant trousers
A sun hat, a T-shirt and sandals
A woolly hat, tracksuit bottoms and trainers
129150.e: The chainsaw is loud and dangerous. A helmet, ear protection and special trousers protect the forestry worker.
129150.m: Protective clothing protects you during dangerous work.

129151.q: Who moves heavy loads through the air on a building site?
129151.e: Crane operators sit high up in the cab and lift heavy parts such as concrete slabs into place.
129151.m: The crane lifts the heavy things.

129152.q: Who puts the tiles on the roof?
129152.e: Roofers cover the roof with tiles. That way the house stays dry.
129152.m: The roofer makes the roof watertight.

129153.q: Where do you get new glasses?
129153.e: Opticians test your eyes and make glasses that suit you.
129153.m: The optician helps you see better.

129154.q: Which job is particularly well known and famous in Switzerland?
129154.e: Switzerland is known all over the world for its watches. Watchmakers build and repair them with fine tools.

129155.q: Why does a watchmaker need a magnifying glass?
a: Because the parts in a watch are very small
Because otherwise she can't hear anything
129155.e: A watch has tiny wheels and screws. With the magnifying glass the watchmaker sees them big.
129155.m: A magnifying glass makes small things big.

129156.q: What does a chimney sweep do?
a: Bakes pizza in a wood-fired oven
129156.e: Chimney sweeps clean chimneys and check heating systems so that no fires start.
129156.m: The chimney sweep keeps the chimney clean.

129157.q: What colour is a chimney sweep's work clothing traditionally?
129157.e: Chimney sweeps traditionally wear black clothes. Soot from the chimney shows less on them.

129158.q: What does a baker need to make dough?
129158.e: For bread you mainly need flour, water, salt and yeast. The yeast makes the dough rise.
129158.m: Flour, water, salt and yeast: that's how bread is made.

129159.q: Who makes fine gateaux, cakes and chocolates?
129159.e: Pastry chefs are experts in sweet things. They make gateaux, cakes and chocolates.
129159.m: Sweet things come from the pastry chef.

129160.q: Which jobs work together when a new house is built?
129160.e: A house needs many jobs: bricklayers build the walls, carpenters the roof, electricians the electrics and painters the colour.

129161.q: Why do some nurses also work at night?
a: Because sick people need help at night too
Because the hospital is tidied up at night
Because they want to sleep during the day
Because more visitors come at night
129161.e: In a hospital there must always be people there, at night and at weekends too. That is why there are shifts.
129161.m: In hospital, help is there round the clock.

129162.q: Which statement about jobs is true?
a: Girls and boys can learn any job
Only adults over 40 can learn a job
129162.e: Every job is open to everyone. There are female pilots, female joiners, male nurses and male nursery teachers.
129162.m: Every job is there for everyone.

129163.q: Who builds and repairs the roads?
129163.e: Road builders lay new roads, surface them with tarmac and fill holes.
129163.m: The road builder makes the way smooth.

129164.q: Who drives the goods by road from the warehouse to the shops?
129164.e: Lorry drivers, officially road transport specialists, drive goods from warehouses to shops.
129164.m: The lorry brings the goods to the shop.

129165.q: Who makes sure everything in the school building is clean and in good repair?
129165.e: Caretakers look after the school building, repair small things and keep everything in order.
129165.m: The caretaker looks after the school building.

129166.e: In the library you can borrow books. The librarian sorts the books and helps you find them.
129166.m: Librarians help you in the library.

129167.q: Dad pays in a restaurant and says to the waitress: “Keep the change.” What does he mean?
a: She may keep the change as a tip
The food was seasoned just right
He wants the change in coins
The bill should be counted again
129167.e: With “Keep the change” you say that the staff may keep the rest of the money. This little thank-you is called a tip.
129167.m: “Keep the change” means the rest is a thank-you.

129168.q: Lea gets a voucher from a bookshop for her birthday. What can she do with it?
a: Pay with it in the bookshop like money
Change it for cash at a cash machine
Shop in any shop in the world
Use it as a bus ticket
129168.e: A voucher is a piece of paper or a card with a value. You can pay with it in the shop named on it, but usually not anywhere else.
129168.m: A voucher is money for one particular shop.

129169.q: The game Noah wants to buy says “sold out” in the shop. What does that mean?
a: You may only look at the game
129169.e: “Sold out” means all of them have already been sold. Noah has to wait until the shop gets new ones, or look somewhere else.

129170.q: When in the year is World Savings Day, when many banks invite children to save?
129170.e: World Savings Day is at the end of October. Many banks invite children to empty their money boxes and bring the money to their account.
129170.m: World Savings Day is at the end of October.

129171.q: What can you keep in a safe deposit box at the bank?
129171.e: A safe deposit box is a small lockable box in a secure room at the bank. People put valuables in it that are not safe enough at home.
129171.m: Valuables go in the safe deposit box.

129172.q: How is a lot of cash taken safely to a bank?
a: In an ordinary letter by post
In the boot of a taxi
129172.e: For large amounts of cash there are special vehicles with thick walls and well-trained drivers. That way the money is well protected on the way.
129172.m: Lots of cash travels in an armoured van.

a: A paper roll with the same number of identical coins
A machine that makes new coins
129173.e: A coin roll always holds the same number of coins of the same kind. That way you can count lots of small change quickly and carry it neatly.
129173.m: A coin roll keeps coins neatly together.

129174.q: In the past, children at the bank often got a savings book. What was written in it?
a: How much money is in the savings account
The names of all the bank staff
129174.e: The bank wrote every deposit and withdrawal in the savings book. That way you could always see how much you had saved. Today you often see this in an app.
129174.m: The savings book showed how much had been saved.

129175.q: The Keller family is going on holiday to Italy. Where can they change francs into euros?
a: At a bank or bureau de change
129175.e: In Italy people pay with euros. Banks and bureaux de change exchange francs for euros.
129175.m: You can change money at the bank.

129176.q: Why do you sometimes have to sign something at the bank?
a: So the bank knows how old you are
So you don't forget your name
129176.e: With a signature you write your name in a special way. It confirms that you want something and agree to it.

129177.q: What does the bank use to count lots of banknotes quickly?
129177.e: A money-counting machine runs the notes through at lightning speed and counts them. It often even notices when a note is fake.
129177.m: The machine counts notes faster than any hand.

129178.q: What does a power of attorney for a bank account mean?
a: Another person may also use the account
The account then belongs to the other person
The bank may close the account
129178.e: With a power of attorney, the account holder allows another person to make payments, for example. But the money still belongs to the holder.
129178.m: Power of attorney means: someone else may act for me.

129179.q: What is special about a cooperative bank?
a: It always belongs to the federal government
It has no accounts of its own
129179.e: At a cooperative bank you can buy shares and become a member of the cooperative. The members can then have a say.
129179.m: In a cooperative, the bank belongs to its members.

129180.q: What is the BIC, also called the SWIFT code, used for in a payment abroad?
a: It is the password for online banking
129180.e: The BIC is an international code for a bank. For payments abroad, it helps send the money to the right bank.
129180.m: The IBAN names the account, the BIC the bank.

129181.q: What is a foreign currency account?
a: An account in euros instead of francs, for example
An account only foreigners may open
An account without an account number
129181.e: A foreign currency account holds money in another currency, such as euros or dollars. That is handy if you often pay or receive money in that currency.
129181.m: Foreign currency account: foreign money, your own account.

a: An account that belongs to several people
An account of the whole municipality
An account run by the school
129182.e: A joint account is in the name of two or more people, for example a couple or flatmates. All holders can use it, depending on what has been agreed.

129183.q: Where can you turn free of charge in Switzerland if you have a dispute with your bank?
a: The SIX stock exchange in Zurich
129183.e: The Swiss Banking Ombudsman is a neutral mediation service. It helps customers free of charge to settle a dispute with a bank without going to court.
129183.m: Dispute with your bank? Go to the ombudsman first.

a: A loan for which securities serve as collateral
A loan only for trips to Italy
A loan secured by your house
129184.e: With a Lombard loan you pledge securities such as shares or bonds. If their value falls sharply, the bank can ask for extra security.

129185.q: What is stored at the ZEK, the Swiss Central Office for Credit Information?
a: Details of loans, leasing and card agreements
The balances of all savings accounts
129185.e: The ZEK collects details of loans, leasing agreements and card accounts, and also of payment defaults. Banks check there before giving a new loan.
129185.m: If you do not pay, you leave traces at the ZEK.

129186.q: What usually happens to the account of a person who has died?
a: It is blocked until the heirs are proven
The money goes straight to the bank
Anyone with the card may withdraw money
129186.e: When the bank learns of the death, it usually blocks the account. Only with proof, for example a certificate of inheritance, can the heirs use it.
129186.m: After a death, the certificate of inheritance decides, not the card.

a: A note from the doctor saying you were ill
129187.e: In a doctor's certificate, the doctor confirms that someone was ill and could not go to school or work. Adults often need it for their employer.
129187.m: A doctor's certificate shows: I really was ill.

129188.q: Your friend is ill in bed. What do you wish her?
129188.e: With “Get well soon”, you wish someone who is ill that they will soon be healthy again. A card or a phone call can cheer them up.
129188.m: Someone who is ill is pleased to hear “Get well soon”.

a: She helps you move well again with exercises
She sells medicines in the pharmacy
She cleans teeth at the surgery
129189.e: After an injury or when you are in pain, the physiotherapist shows you exercises. They make muscles and joints strong and flexible again.
129189.m: Physio means practising until it works again.

129190.q: Mia has a cough. Her brother still has tablets from the doctor. May she just take them?
a: No, they are only meant for her brother
Yes, a cough is always the same
Yes, if she only takes two
129190.e: The doctor chooses a medicine and the amount specially for one person. For another child it can be wrong or even dangerous.

a: A village fair with rides and stalls
A song you sing in the evening
A cow with a big bell
129191.e: A Chilbi is a cheerful fair in a village or town. There are roundabouts, bumper cars, stalls with sweets and candyfloss.
129191.m: At the Chilbi everything goes round and round.

129192.q: Which sweet, brown treat in small pieces do people often buy at markets in Switzerland?
129192.e: Magenbrot is small pieces of gingerbread dough with a shiny, sweet glaze. People like to buy it in a little bag at markets and at the Chilbi.

129193.q: What is the gingerbread with an almond filling from the Appenzell region called?
129193.e: The Appenzeller Biber is a gingerbread filled with almond paste. A picture, for example a bear, is often pressed onto it.
129193.m: Although “Biber” is German for beaver, here it is gingerbread, not an animal.

129194.q: What colour are the post boxes of Swiss Post?
129194.e: Swiss Post's letter boxes are yellow, just like the PostBuses. That makes them easy to spot everywhere.
129194.m: The post in Switzerland is yellow.

129195.q: Which German municipality is completely surrounded by Swiss territory?
129195.e: Büsingen belongs to Germany but lies in the middle of the canton of Schaffhausen. Such an area is called an exclave. People there often pay in francs.
129195.m: Büsingen: German, but surrounded by Switzerland.

129196.q: How do most voters in Switzerland cast their vote?
a: By raising their hand in the village square
By sending a text to the Federal Council
129196.e: The great majority vote by post. You fill in the ballot paper at home and send it to the municipality in good time with your voting card.

129197.q: Which canton does the number plate code “AI” stand for?
129197.e: Every canton has a two-letter code. AI stands for Appenzell Innerrhoden, AR for Appenzell Ausserrhoden, AG for Aargau and UR for Uri.
129197.m: AI is Innerrhoden, AR is Ausserrhoden.

129198.q: In which two cantons is Italian an official language?
129198.e: In Ticino, Italian is the only official language. In the Grisons it is one of three official languages, for example in the southern valleys such as the Misox and the Puschlav.
129198.m: Italian: Ticino and part of the Grisons.

129199.q: From which place does the cable car up the Säntis leave?
129199.e: The valley station of the Säntis cable car is on the Schwägalp in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden. From there the cabin glides up to the highest mountain of the Alpstein.
129199.m: You go up the Säntis from the Schwägalp.

129200.q: What happens at the “Chesslete” in Solothurn?
a: Carnival begins early in the morning with lots of noise
People celebrate the grape harvest by the lake
Decorated cows go up to the alpine pasture
129200.e: The Chesslete opens the Solothurn carnival early in the morning on the Thursday before Lent. Many people wear white nightshirts and make noise to drive away the winter.
129200.m: Chesslete: noise in the morning, carnival begins.

129201.q: What is the Knabenschiessen in Zurich?
a: A shooting competition for young people in September
A football tournament only for boys
A fireworks display on New Year's Eve
A rowing race on Lake Zurich
129201.e: At the Knabenschiessen, young people compete in shooting, today both girls and boys. There is also a big fair at the Albisgüetli.
129201.m: In September young people in Zurich shoot to become the shooting king.

129202.q: What is the last, deciding bout at a Schwingen festival called?
129202.e: In the Schlussgang the best wrestlers face each other. Whoever wins it has a good chance of winning the festival or even the title of king.
